## Location, helper and caller

The implementation is in **`packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts`**, inside the request-preparation module `LLMRequestPrep` (module alias at line 228). The actual filter is the local helper **`resolveTools`** (lines 210–216); it is called by **`prepare`** (declared line 56) at line 148: `const tools = resolveTools(input)`. `prepare` in turn is called from `LLM.run` in **`packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts:106–113`** (stream entry `LLM.run`, line 85), which spreads its `StreamInput` (`user`, `tools`, `permission` at llm.ts:35–47) into the prepare input (`PrepareInput` in request.ts:20–36). Session-level permission rules reach it via `permission: session.permission` at **`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:1275`**.

## The filter itself

```ts
210 function resolveTools(input: Pick<PrepareInput, "tools" | "agent" | "permission" | "user">) {
211   const disabled = Permission.disabled(
212     Object.keys(input.tools),
213     Permission.merge(input.agent.permission, input.permission ?? []),
214   )
215   return Record.filter(input.tools, (_, k) => input.user.tools?.[k] !== false && !disabled.has(k))
216 }
```

So an already-built tool key is kept only if the per-message toggle is not literally `false` **and** it is not in the `disabled` set. Because the test is `!== false`, only `false` excludes; `true`, `undefined`, or an absent entry keep the tool. The toggle lives on the user message: `PrepareInput.user: SessionV1.User` (request.ts:21), and the session-message schema declares `tools: Schema.optional(Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Boolean))` at **`packages/schema/src/v1/session.ts:353`**.

## Permission merge order

`Permission.merge` is a flat concatenation: `rulesets.flat()` (**`packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:200–202`**). `resolveTools` passes **agent permissions first, then `input.permission` (session/request) second** (request.ts:213). Because rule selection uses `findLast` (below), the later ruleset wins whenever rules overlap, i.e. session/request permission overrides the agent's for the same permission key.

## Rule choice and disabling

**`packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:204–214`** implements `Permission.disabled`:

```ts
205 const edits = ["edit", "write", "apply_patch"]
206 const reads = ["list_mcp_resources", "list_mcp_resource_templates", "read_mcp_resource"]
207 return new Set(tools.filter((tool) => {
208   const permission = edits.includes(tool) ? "edit" : reads.includes(tool) ? "read" : tool
209   const rule = ruleset.findLast((rule) => Wildcard.match(permission, rule.permission))
210   return rule?.pattern === "*" && rule.action === "deny"
211 }))
```

For each tool name, a permission key is computed: editing tools map to `"edit"`, MCP-resource-reading tools map to `"read"`, everything else uses its own name. The rule is chosen as the **last** entry in the flattened ruleset whose `permission` field wildcard-matches that key. The tool is disabled only when the chosen rule has pattern exactly `"*"` **and** action `"deny"`. If no rule matches (`rule` is `undefined`) or a deny uses a narrower pattern, the tool is not removed from the request's tool map. `Wildcard.match` converts the pattern to a regex (`*`→`.*`, `?`→`.`, escaped punctuation; case-insensitive only on Windows) and anchors it — **`packages/core/src/util/wildcard.ts:3–13`**.

## Grouping of edit and MCP-read names

- Editing names: `edit`, `write`, `apply_patch` → permission `"edit"` (permission/index.ts:205, 208).
- MCP resource names: `list_mcp_resources`, `list_mcp_resource_templates`, `read_mcp_resource` → permission `"read"` (permission/index.ts:206, 208). These correspond to the MCP resource tool family registered via `MCP_RESOURCE_TOOLS` in **`packages/opencode/src/session/tools.ts:27`** (uses at lines 140, 222, 305).

## Boundary

This is request-shaping only: it decides which entries of the already-assembled `input.tools` map are exposed to the model; it does not inspect tool arguments or execute anything. The filtered map is later sorted into the prepared request (request.ts:184), and Copilot-only `_noop` compatibility injection occurs after filtering if the map is empty (request.ts:159–175). Per-pattern ask/deny enforcement on individual invocations is separate (`Permission.ask`/`evaluate`, permission/index.ts:28–38, 67–84).

Limitations: I did not read the surrounding schema context for `packages/schema/src/v1/session.ts:353` (only the grep line), nor the value side of `MCP_RESOURCE_TOOLS`; the name correspondence above is based on the matched literal names in `Permission.disabled` and the `MCP_RESOURCE_TOOLS.*` usage sites.
